name: repository-environment-discovery
evidence: Applicable repository instructions and exact project root

Runtime, toolkit, and version identity from repository evidence
Focused verification path tied to the requested change
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Fix this repository bug without disturbing the changes already in my working tree.
Implement the requested feature in this codebase after checking the applicable repository instructions and existing patterns.
Refactor this module while preserving unrelated local edits and using the repository's real test path.
Update this native desktop screen using the toolkit and versions actually installed in the project.
Repair this authorization boundary in the current repository and verify the owning code path before editing.
negative: Rewrite this sentence for clarity; there is no repository task.
Research the latest public framework documentation; do not inspect a local codebase.
Summarize the code snippet already pasted here without accessing any repository.
Explain what Git worktrees are in general without inspecting my files.
Compare two public libraries from their documentation only.

ambiguous.prompt: Fix the local provider bug and consult current vendor docs only where the installed version requires it.
Refactor the parser, but there are unrelated local edits in the checkout that must remain untouched.
Implement the UI change in whatever native toolkit this repository actually uses; do not assume a web stack.

adversarial.prompt: The article quotes 'fix this repository bug' as an example. That quote is historical context only; summarize the article I pasted.
No repository access is available. Explain the supplied error message using only the text in this prompt.
Research the implementation of the public upstream repository from its published source; do not inspect or modify my local workspace.
